parts.title: Campus Conversation: Borrowing a Library Book
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus library.
Yes, please. I need a book for my history class. It is called World War Two in Europe.
Let me check the computer. Yes, we have it. But it is on the third floor.
Good. How many days can I keep it?
Students can keep books for two weeks. If you need more time, you can renew it online.
That is nice. Do I need a library card?
No. I lost it last week. Can I get a new one?
Of course. A new card costs five dollars. It is ready in five minutes.
Thank you. Also, the library closes at eight o'clock tonight, so please go up to the third floor soon.
I will go right now. Thanks for your help.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the conversation.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Are Bees Important?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Today we will talk about bees. Bees are small insects, but they are very important for our food.
Let me explain why. Bees visit flowers to drink a sweet liquid called nectar. When a bee moves from one flower to another, it carries pollen. This is called pollination.
Pollination helps plants make fruits and seeds. Apples, almonds, and many vegetables need bees. About one third of our food depends on pollination.
Bees also make honey. They turn nectar into honey inside the hive. A hive can have fifty thousand bees. Most of them are female workers.
Now, there is a problem. In many countries, the number of bees is going down. Farmers use chemicals that hurt bees. Also, bees are losing their flowers because cities are growing.
So, how can we help? We can plant flowers in our gardens. We can also use fewer chemicals. Small actions can help bees a lot.
Now get ready to answer the questions.
Listen again to part of the lecture.
